rows.source_table: Applicant Table 123 'Summary of Completed Exposure-Safety Analyses' (printed p422), row 'Grade 3/4 Thrombocytopenia / MDS3001 / Univariate', Cmax column
rows.notes: Statistically significant positive exposure-response between Cycle 1 Cmax and Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia in MDS3001 (pLRT=0.0192 univariate, 0.0195 multivariate). Same table: AUC 0.0894 univariate / 0.0594 multivariate (trend only), Cavg 0.998 (no relationship). CRITICAL CONTRAST: for Grade 3/4 NEUTROPENIA in MDS3001 no exposure metric was significant (Cmax 0.145, AUC 0.827, Cavg 0.749) - the exposure-driven cytopenia is specifically the platelet one. Recovery endpoints showed no E-R (Cmax p=0.884 for <2wk, 0.869 for <4wk resolution).

rows.exposure_duration: Cycle 1 Cmax, pooled across all imetelstat studies
rows.effect_vs_control: positive E-R confirmed in the pooled dataset (univariate and multivariate)
rows.source_table: Applicant Table 123 (printed p422), row 'Grade 3/4 Thrombocytopenia / All / Univariate and Multivariate', log10-Cmax column
rows.notes: Pooled-dataset replication: log10 Cmax pLRT <0.0001 univariate AND <0.0001 multivariate; log10 AUC 0.581 univariate but 0.00139 multivariate; Cavg 0.184 (NS). Confirms the MDS3001-only finding at much larger N and over a wider exposure range. Cmax, not AUC or Cavg, is the driving metric - consistent with an acute per-infusion peak-driven effect on megakaryocyte progenitors.

rows.source_table: Applicant Table 124 'Summary Statistics of the Final Multiple Logistic Regression for Proportion of Subjects with Grade 3/4 Thrombocytopenia (Study MDS3001)' (printed p426), row '*Cmax'
rows.notes: Final multivariate logistic model. Cmax slope 0.0166 (SE 0.00740, statistic 2.24, p=0.0252); intercept 0.717 (p=0.347); the only other retained covariate is BASELINE PLATELET COUNT, slope -0.00632 (95% CI -0.00952 to -0.00353, SE 0.00152, statistic -4.15, p=0.0000327) - i.e. lower baseline platelets independently and very strongly predict Grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia, more strongly than exposure does. FDA conclusion (printed p429): 'higher imetelstat Cmax is correlated with higher incidence of Grade 3/4 Thrombocytopenia'. The FDA added a statement to labelling section 12.2 that higher exposure gives higher incidence of grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia (printed p351), and issued PMR #5 requiring a randomised trial of at least two dosages (printed p358).

rows.source_table: Figure 36 'MDS3001-Phase 3: Platelet count by study arm at baseline and during treatment' (printed p287) + accompanying text
rows.notes: readout_value deliberately TBD: Figure 36 is a plotted mean +/- SE curve with NO printed data table, so no numeric value is reproduced. The source's own words are recorded instead: 'mean platelet count was similar between arms initially but decreased in the imetelstat arm while staying constant in the placebo arm during treatment. Of note, the mean platelet count in the imetelstat arm decreased to grade 1 thrombocytopenia and remained in this range throughout the study.' Graded 1 on that explicit statement (arm-level MEAN reaching only CTCAE Grade 1). Approximate visual reading of the plot, NOT used as a value: imetelstat baseline ~250 falling to a ~100-120 x10^9/L plateau from ~week 9 onward, placebo flat at ~210-240. Denominators printed under the figure (imetelstat 118 at baseline falling to 51 by week 49-52; placebo 60 to 19).

rows.source_table: Figure 4 'MDS3001-Phase 3: Positive exposure-response relationship between imetelstat exposure and Grade 3-4 thrombocytopenia' (printed p90); duplicated as Applicant Figure 54 (printed p425)
rows.notes: readout_value TBD BY DESIGN. The figure plots median +/- 95% CI probability of Grade 3+ thrombocytopenia for each of four Cycle 1 Cmax quartiles against a fitted logistic curve, but NO quartile values are printed anywhere in the document, so none are reproduced. Approximate visual reading, recorded as context only and NOT as data: the four quartile medians rise from roughly 50% at ~65 ug/mL to roughly 70% at ~120 ug/mL, with the fitted curve running ~45% at 40 ug/mL to ~85% at 175 ug/mL. Human reference exposure: popPK-predicted Cmax 89.2 ug/mL at the approved 7.1 mg/kg dose (printed p48). Quantitative values for this relationship should be taken from the Table 123/124 rows instead.

rows.source_table: Section 20 Labeling Recommendations table, 'Warnings and Precautions - Thrombocytopenia (5.1)' row (printed p345)
rows.notes: THE LABELLED FIGURE. Proposed/agreed US PI section 5.1 text as reproduced in the review: 'New or worsening Grade 3 or 4 thrombocytopenia, based on laboratory values, occurred in 65.2% of MDS patients treated with [Rytelo]. Median time to onset: 6 weeks.' FDA modified the Applicant's proposal to recommend monitoring blood counts weekly for the first 2 cycles and before and 7-10 days after each subsequent cycle. Section 2.3 dose modification directs holding treatment when platelets are less than 50 x10^9/L, with first dose reduction to 5.6 mg/kg and second to 4.4 mg/kg q4w (printed p343-344). Thrombocytopenia is a Warning and Precaution, NOT a boxed warning.

The events-per-patient ratio 212/77 is arithmetic on the two printed counts.

rows.source_table: Table 98 'Hemorrhagic events in patients on MDS3001 by study arm and severity' (printed p308), row 'Any Hemorrhage', All Grade column
rows.notes: Any-grade haemorrhage, NOT conditioned on platelet count. Graded 1: modest excess over placebo (+10.2 RD) driven by mild events - epistaxis 7% vs 0%, hematoma 6% vs 0%. Component cells: GI haemorrhage 4.2% vs 3.4% (RD +0.8); contusion 0.8% vs 5% (RD -3.4, i.e. LOWER on drug).

rows.source_table: Table 98 (printed p308), row 'Any Hemorrhage', Grade 3-4 column
rows.notes: DELIBERATELY GRADED 1, NOT 3. Severe haemorrhage occurred in only 3 imetelstat patients (2.5%) versus 1 placebo patient (1.7%) - a risk difference of +0.8, i.e. essentially the background rate in this population. Per the rubric's explicit warning, grading this 3 on the word 'haemorrhage' would manufacture a severe signal out of a near-null result. All Grade 3-4 events were GI bleeding except one Grade 3 haematuria; the Grade 3-4 GI-haemorrhage cell is 1.7% in BOTH arms (RD exactly 0). No fatal haemorrhage occurred in MDS3001 - though the clinical reviewer judged one Phase 2 death attributed to 'neurological degeneration' to be consistent with unconfirmed intracranial haemorrhage (printed p309).

rows.source_table: Table 98 (printed p308), row 'Contusion', All Grade and Grade 3-4 columns
rows.notes: NEGATIVE / BELOW-PLACEBO ROW - grade 0. Contusion, the classic bruising manifestation of thrombocytopenia, was reported LESS often on imetelstat (0.8%, 1 patient) than on placebo (5%), risk difference -3.4; zero Grade 3-4 contusions in either arm. The reviewer notes contusion was the one haemorrhage term NOT more common on drug. Kept explicitly so the null cells in this table are not lost.

rows.source_table: Table 99 'Thrombocytopenia and hemorrhagic events by dose level in the overall development program' (printed p309), row 'Thrombocytopenia', Low dose N=54
rows.notes: DOSE-RESPONSE BACKBONE row 1/3 for thrombocytopenia. Dose bands are printed as Low/Standard/High; the review defines them elsewhere as <7.1, 7.1 and >7.1 mg/kg per 4 weeks (printed p223 '<7.1 mg/kg and >7.1 mg/kg groups ... compared to the 7.1 mg/kg group'; printed p309 '>7.1 mg/kg/4 weeks'). Bands recorded verbatim rather than converted to invented midpoints. Any-grade AE term -> grade 1. Even the lowest dose band exceeds placebo. The same cell appears as 11 (20) in Table 73 (printed p271) - identical count, different percentage rounding.

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Fatal hemorrhage', High dose N=296
rows.notes: Graded 3 - death. Fatal haemorrhage occurs ONLY in the supra-recommended dose band. The 5 fatal events are itemised in the text: haemorrhage, intracranial haemorrhage (2), oesophageal varices haemorrhage, and upper GI haemorrhage (printed p309). Together with the two grade-0 zero cells above, this row makes the fatal-bleeding dose-threshold explicit: 0 / 0 / 1.7%.

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Fatal hemorrhage', Low dose N=54
rows.notes: EXPLICIT ZERO - grade 0, and evidence. Had events occurred this band would have carried grade 3 (death from haemorrhage). Preserves the denominator (N=54) at the bottom of the fatal-bleeding dose-response.

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Fatal hemorrhage', Standard dose N=190
rows.notes: EXPLICIT ZERO - grade 0. IMPORTANT SAFETY POINT: at the APPROVED 7.1 mg/kg q4w dose, across 190 patients in the whole development programme, there were no fatal haemorrhages, despite a 73% thrombocytopenia rate. Would have carried grade 3 had events occurred.

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Grade 3-4 hemorrhage', High dose N=296
rows.notes: Graded 3 and the top of a clean monotonic severe-bleeding dose-response: 1.9% -> 6% -> 21% across the three dose bands against 1.7% placebo. Text confirms: 'grade 3-4 hemorrhagic events were seen in 62 (21%) patients ... who received >7.1 mg/kg/4 weeks' (printed p309).

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Grade 3-4 hemorrhage', Low dose N=54
rows.notes: GRADED 1 NOT 3 - a single severe bleed at 1.9% versus 1.7% on placebo is the background rate, not a drug-induced platelet injury. Per the rubric, bleeding is graded on attribution and this cell shows essentially no excess. This is the low anchor of the severe-bleeding dose-response (1.9% -> 6% -> 21%).

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Grade 3-4 hemorrhage', Standard dose N=190
rows.notes: Graded 3: severe haemorrhagic events at ~3.5x the placebo rate in a population with a 73% thrombocytopenia rate at the same dose band - a genuine excess of severe bleeding, unlike the low-dose cell.

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Hemorrhage', High dose N=296
rows.notes: Any-grade haemorrhage by dose band, row 3/3, and the endpoint where the dose-response IS monotonic (22% -> 26% -> 52% vs 12% placebo). Graded 2 rather than 1 because the excess over placebo is large (+40 points) and actionable, unlike the low/standard bands. Related text: 138 patients receiving >7.1 mg/kg/4 weeks had at least one broad-SMQ haemorrhage event; removing laboratory terms leaves 98 (33%) (printed p309).

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Hemorrhage', Low dose N=54
rows.notes: Any-grade haemorrhage (broad SMQ) by dose band, row 1/3. Not conditioned on platelet count. Graded 1 (any-grade, modest excess over the 12% placebo rate).

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Hemorrhage', Standard dose N=190
rows.notes: Any-grade haemorrhage by dose band, row 2/3. Graded 1 (any-grade).

rows.source_table: Table 99 (printed p309), row 'Thrombocytopenia', High dose N=296
rows.notes: DOSE-RESPONSE BACKBONE row 3/3. NON-MONOTONIC: the AE-term incidence is LOWER in the high-dose band (62%) than the standard-dose band (73%), which the reviewer attributes to confounding by underlying disease - the high-dose band is dominated by solid-tumour and non-MDS haematologic-malignancy studies while the standard-dose band is largely MDS ('the relationship is confounded by the wide variety of underlying conditions being treated', printed p309; 'patients with MDS are more vulnerable to cytopenias compared to patients with solid tumors', printed p284). The dose-response IS monotonic for the haemorrhage endpoints in the same table.
